release_notes: Build 102 replaces the final duplicate-path blocker in the completed C: archive workflow with safe physical-folder grouping.
When several Quiz History rows point to the same physical C: project folder, Factburst now treats that folder as one archive unit instead of trying to guess which History row owns it.
Every linked History row must have all required uploads complete before the shared physical folder can move; otherwise the whole folder stays on C:.
The project is copied to Z: once and verified once, or an existing same-name Z: copy is reused only when the complete relative file set has a strong verified copy identity.
All linked Quiz History paths are updated together in one SQLite transaction and individually verified before any C: deletion is attempted.

Shared physical-project rows are explicitly registered so the database uniqueness guard still blocks unrelated duplicate paths while allowing the verified rows from one physical project to share their Z: path.
If the grouped database update cannot be verified, Factburst attempts to roll the group back to the original C: path and keeps the physical C: folder.
Existing Z: folders are never overwritten or deleted; new collisions continue to use archived-copy numbering.
The Archive completed C confirmation and progress screens now report physical folders separately from the number of linked Quiz History rows.
